Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players. It will be the pairing of skipper Laura Wolvaardt and Tazmin Brits to open the innings for South Africa Women. Renuka Singh Thakur has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, 144 is the target that is needed for South Africa Women to get a win under their belt heading into the main event. India Women have the quality and depth in their spin attack to defend this total but a lot will depend on how the Powerplay goes for both sides. Stick around as the chase is up next.

With how things started, South Africa Women would have wanted to control the first innings a bit better but are well and truly in the game. Ayabonga Khaka was excellent up top in the absence of Marizanne Kapp and Chloe Tryon too bowled a tight spell from the other end. They bowled decently in the middle overs and did manage to pick up a couple of quick wickets but went for a few too many runs in the last few overs. Khaka finished off things on a high, claiming 3 more scalps in the final over to make it a fine five-wicket haul.

A good fightback from the Indian middle order yet again but South Africa Women will be fairly happy with how things have panned out so far. India Women defended 141 in the last game and once again they have a similar sort of a total on board. India Women were put into bat but Shafali Verma departed for a duck and skipper Harmanpreet Kaur didn't hang around for much either. It was the stand between Smriti Mandhana and Jemimah Rodrigues worth 40 runs that provided some stability. However, the duo departed in the space of a few balls, and then came the blitz towards the latter part as Deepti Sharma and Richa Ghosh as they added on 70 runs and got India to a par score.
Bowls a yorker on the stumps and Arundhati Reddy walks in to flick it towards mid-wicket to get a single off the last ball. India Women finish at 144/7 after 20 overs.

India Women come into this contest on the back of a good win against West Indies Women but it wasn't all smooth sailing. The top 3 failed miserably and they leaked runs towards the end with the ball as well. The middle order is strong but they will be looking for a much better start with the bat this time around.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the Women's T20 World Cup, 2024 warm-up games. It is time for the final round of warm-up games to get underway before the main event kicks off in a couple of days time. South Africa Women now take on India Women at the ICC Academy Stadium in Dubai.
... MATCH DAY ...

The last day of warm-up fixtures is here, and in one of the three matches scheduled, India will face South Africa at the ICC Academy in Dubai. Both teams will be eager for a win to build momentum heading into the main event. South Africa, in particular, are looking to bounce back after a disappointing defeat against New Zealand in their first warm-up game. They struggled against spin and were bowled out for just 92 runs, with seven wickets falling to spin. Marizanne Kapp did not feature in that match, but players like Laura Wolvaardt, Tazmin Brits, and Sune Luus will be keen to deliver improved performances, especially against spin, which they are likely to encounter frequently during the tournament. On the bowling front, defending 93 runs was a challenging task, so if they win the toss against India, they may opt to bowl first to allow bowlers like Ayabonga Khaka, Nonkululeko Mlaba, Marizanne Kapp, and Chloe Tryon to get some overs under their belt. As for India, in their game against West Indies, after a shaky start, Jemimah Rodrigues' fifty kept them afloat and then a collective effort helped them close out the game. The top three of Shafali Verma, Smriti Mandhana and Harmanpreet Kaur could not have any sort of impact and will be eager to enter the tournament with a significant score under their belt. On the bowling front, the new ball pairing of Pooja Vastrakar and Renuka Singh Thakur excelled but a worrying factor was Shreyanka Patil and Radha Yadav going for plenty in their overs. Deepti Sharma and Asha Sobhana were tidy and the likes of Patil and Yadav would want to get that confidence back in them with an improved showing. Who are you backing to come out on top?
